questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.topic: Judgment as a matter of law
questions.question:
A retailer brought a federal diversity action against a wholesaler, alleging breach of contract and fraudulent misrepresentation. After the parties presented their evidence at trial, the court instructed the jury on the law. Neither party filed a motion for judgment as a matter of law before the case went to the jury.
The jury found for the retailer on both claims. After the court entered judgment on the verdict, the wholesaler moved for a new trial and for judgment as a matter of law, arguing that the evidence was insufficient to support the jury verdict on either claim. The court acknowledged that there had been problems with some of the evidence, but it denied the motions. The wholesaler appealed, challenging the sufficiency of the evidence.
Should the appellate court consider the wholesaler's challenge?

choices.A: No, because a determination of the sufficiency of the evidence is solely within the jury's province.
choices.B: No, because the wholesaler did not raise the sufficiency-of-the-evidence issue in a motion for judgment as a matter of law before the case went to the jury.
choices.C: Yes, because, as the trial court acknowledged, the wholesaler has strong arguments on the challenge.
choices.D: Yes, because the challenge was raised and ruled on by the trial court before the wholesaler filed the appeal.

A party may challenge on appeal the sufficiency of the evidence supporting the jury's verdict so long as that party made the appropriate motions during and after trial. To preserve a sufficiency-of-the-evidence issue for appeal, Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 50 requires that a party do the following:

  • Before the case is submitted to the jury, move for judgment as a matter of law (JMOL)—ie, a judgment entered in favor of the movant because the evidence is legally insufficient for a reasonable jury to find in the nonmovant's favor
  • Within 28 days after the entry of final judgment, file a renewed motion for JMOL—the party may also include an alternative or joint request for a new trial with this motion

Here, the wholesaler moved for JMOL and a new trial after the court entered judgment on the jury's verdict. However, the wholesaler did not raise the sufficiency-of-the-evidence issue in a motion for JMOL before the case went to the jury as required by FRCP 50. As a result, the wholesaler did not preserve this issue for appeal, and the appellate court should not consider the wholesaler's challenge.

(Choice A) A determination of the sufficiency of the evidence is not solely within the jury's province because the trial and appellate court may assess whether the evidence was legally sufficient to support the verdict.

(Choice B) No, because the wholesaler did not raise the sufficiency-of-the-evidence issue in a motion for judgment as a matter of law before the case went to the jury.

(Choices C & D) The trial court acknowledged that the wholesaler has strong arguments for challenging the sufficiency of the evidence and ruled on the wholesaler's posttrial motions.* However, the appellate court cannot consider that challenge because the wholesaler failed to move for JMOL before the case was submitted to the jury.

*Technically, the trial court erred in considering the merits of the wholesaler's motion for JMOL since the motion was not made before the case was submitted to the jury.

📌 Educational Objective

A party may challenge on appeal the sufficiency of the evidence supporting the jury's verdict if that party (1) moved for judgment as a matter of law (JMOL) before the case was submitted to the jury and (2) renewed its motion for JMOL within 28 days after the entry of judgment.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(a) (motion for judgment as a matter of law).
  • Unitherm Food Sys., Inc. v. Swift-Eckrich, Inc., 546 U.S. 394, 399–402 (2006) (explaining the procedural requirements to challenge the sufficiency of evidence supporting a jury verdict).
questions.zh-question:
一家零售商对一家批发商提起了联邦多元管辖权之诉，指控其违约和欺诈性虚假陈述。在双方当事人在庭审中出示证据后，法院就法律问题对陪审团进行了指示。在案件提交给陪审团之前，双方均未提出法律上判决的动议。

陪审团在两项诉求上均裁定零售商胜诉。在法院根据陪审团裁决作出判决后，批发商提出进行新审判和法律上判决的动议，辩称证据不足以支持陪审团对任何一项诉求的裁决。法院承认部分证据存在问题，但驳回了这些动议。批发商提起上诉，对证据的充分性提出质疑。

上诉法院是否应审理批发商的质疑？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为确定证据的充分性完全属于陪审团的权限范围。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为在案件提交给陪审团之前，批发商没有在法律上判决的动议中提出证据充分性的问题。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为正如初审法院所承认的，批发商对该质疑有强有力的论据。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为在批发商提起上诉之前，该质疑已由初审法院提出并作出裁定。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure (民事诉讼法)
核心考点：FRCP 50

关于法律上的判决 (Judgment as a Matter of Law, JMOL) 的程序要求：要保留上诉时挑战“证据充分性”的权利，当事人必须严格遵循“两步走”程序。

⚖️ 法律规则解析

根据《联邦民事诉讼规则》第50条 (FRCP 50)，挑战陪审团裁决证据不足的流程是强制性的：

第一步：案件提交陪审团之前
必须提出 JMOL Motion (Rule 50(a))。
⚠️ 本案中批发商错过了这一步！
第二步：判决登记后 28 天内
必须提出 Renewed JMOL Motion (Rule 50(b))。
结果：上诉审查
只有完成了前两步，上诉法院才能审查证据是否充分。

关键原则： 如果一方当事人在案件提交给陪审团之前没有提出 JMOL 动议，他们就放弃 (Waive) 了在审判后提出 Renewed JMOL 的权利，同时也放弃了在上诉中挑战证据充分性的权利。

🔍 案情应用

在本案中，批发商 (Wholesaler) 犯了一个致命的程序错误：

  • 他们在庭审证据出示完毕后，没有立即提出 JMOL 动议。
  • 他们等到陪审团作出裁决后，才试图通过审后动议 (Post-trial motions) 来补救。

根据美国最高法院在 Unitherm Food Sys., Inc. v. Swift-Eckrich, Inc. 中的判例，由于批发商没有在第一阶段提出动议，上诉法院无权 (Powerless) 审查证据的充分性。

✅ 正确答案：B

"No, because the wholesaler did not raise the sufficiency-of-the-evidence issue in a motion for judgment as a matter of law before the case went to the jury."

这是对 FRCP 50 程序要求的直接应用。没有“前置动议”(Pre-verdict motion)，就没有“后置动议”(Post-verdict motion) 的基础，也就没有上诉审查的资格。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A： 错误。证据充分性并非“完全”由陪审团决定。如果程序正确，法官完全有权判定证据在法律上是否不足。

选项 C & D： 错误。虽然初审法官后来确实听取了动议并承认证据有问题，但这不能“治愈” (Cure) 批发商未能在陪审团审议前提出动议的程序性失误。程序性门槛是严格的。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

看到 "Sufficiency of the evidence"（证据充分性）的上诉问题时，立即检查时间线：

Did they move for JMOL BEFORE the jury retired?

如果是 No，那么上诉法院通常不能审理该问题。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A plaintiff sued a defendant in a federal district court for breach of contract. After the trial, the jury returned a verdict in favor of the plaintiff and awarded her $1,000,000. The district court entered a final judgment consistent with the jury's verdict. The defendant then filed a notice of appeal, alleging that the district court abused its discretion by failing to exclude several pieces of evidence during trial. The day after the notice of appeal was filed, the district court discovered that the final judgment listed only a $1,000 award for the plaintiff. The appellate court has not docketed the appeal of the final judgment.
How is the district court likely to proceed?

choices.A: Correct the mistake in the judgment on its own initiative.
choices.B: Instruct the appellate court to correct the mistake in the judgment on appeal.
choices.C: Provide the parties with notice and an opportunity to be heard before correcting the mistake in the judgment.
choices.D: Request permission from the appellate court to correct the mistake in the judgment.

questions.explanation:
Posttrial correction of mistakes
(FRCP 60(a))
Type of mistake Definition Time of correction
Clerical Misstatement of court's intent
  • Eg, court entered judgment for "$10,000" instead of "$100,000"
  • Before appeal docketed: on court's own initiative or by motion
  • After appeal docketed: with appellate court's leave
Oversight/omission Exclusion misrepresents court's intent
  • Eg, judgment failed to include required interest in award
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

FRCP 60 allows a district court to correct a clerical mistake or a mistake arising from an oversight or omission in a judgment, order, or other part of the record. The court may do so on its own initiative (ie, sua sponte) or pursuant to a party's motion before an appeal from the judgment or order is docketed—ie, added to the appellate court's schedule. The appellate court's leave (ie, permission) is only required after the appeal has been docketed.

Here, a clerical mistake occurred since the jury's verdict awarded the plaintiff $1,000,000 but the final judgment awarded her only $1,000. Although the defendant had filed a notice of appeal from the judgment, the appeal has not yet been docketed. Therefore, the district court does not need to obtain the appellate court's permission and likely will correct the mistake on its own initiative (Choice A) Correct the mistake in the judgment on its own initiative.

(Choice B) A district court does not have the power to instruct an appellate court how to act. Instead, appellate courts have the power to review the decisions of district courts within their boundaries and issue instructions that the district court must follow when a case is remanded.

(Choice C) A district court need not provide the parties with notice or an opportunity to be heard before it corrects a mistake in a judgment before an appeal is docketed. Instead, the court may do so on its own initiative.

📌 Educational Objective

A district court may correct a mistake in a judgment, order, or other part of the record on its own initiative or pursuant to a party's motion before an appeal from the judgment or order is docketed. The district court need only obtain the appellate court's leave to correct the mistake after the appeal has been docketed.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 60(a) (correction of mistake in judgment or order).
  • 11 Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2856 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining how a court may correct a mistake after an appeal has been taken).
questions.zh-question:
一名原告在联邦地区法院就违约起诉一名被告。审判后，陪审团作出了有利于原告的裁决，并判给她1,000,000美元的赔偿金。地区法院根据陪审团的裁决作出了最终判决。随后，被告提交了上诉通知，声称地区法院在审判期间未能排除几项证据，滥用了其裁量权。在上诉通知提交后的第二天，地区法院发现最终判决中仅列出给予原告1,000美元的赔偿金。

地区法院可能会如何处理？

zh-choices.A: 依其职权主动纠正判决中的错误。
zh-choices.B: 指示上诉法院在上诉期间纠正判决中的错误。
zh-choices.C: 在纠正判决中的错误之前，向各方当事人发出通知并给予其陈述意见的机会。
zh-choices.D: 请求上诉法院许可，以纠正判决中的错误。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析
判决错误的修正 (FRCP 60(a))

⚖️ 法律规则：FRCP 60(a)

联邦民事诉讼规则第 60(a) 条规定，法院可以随时纠正判决、命令或记录中的笔误 (Clerical Mistakes) 或因疏忽、遗漏造成的错误。

纠正的方式取决于案件是否已进入上诉程序：

阶段 1：上诉登记前 (Before Appeal Docketed)
法院可以依职权主动 (Sua Sponte) 或应一方动议纠正错误。无需上诉法院许可。
阶段 2：上诉登记后 (After Appeal Docketed)
只有在获得上诉法院许可 (Leave of Appellate Court) 后，地区法院才能纠正错误。

📝 本案分析

1. 错误的性质：
陪审团裁定赔偿 $1,000,000，但判决书写成 $1,000。这显然是一个典型的笔误 (Clerical Mistake)，属于 FRCP 60(a) 的管辖范围。

2. 时间节点：
被告刚刚提交了“上诉通知” (Notice of Appeal)。虽然上诉程序启动了，但题目暗示上诉尚未在上一级法院正式登记在册 (Docketed)。

3. 结论：
因为上诉尚未被 Docketed，地区法院仍保留纠正笔误的管辖权。法院无需通知当事人，也无需请求上诉法院许可，即可依职权主动 (on its own initiative) 修正金额。

❌ 选项 B 错误： 地区法院无权“指示”上诉法院如何行动。这是上下级法院关系的倒置。

❌ 选项 C 错误： 对于纯粹的笔误 (Clerical Mistake)，FRCP 60(a) 允许法院在不通知当事人的情况下直接修正。

❌ 选项 D 错误： 只有在上诉已经登记 (Docketed) 后，才需要上诉法院的许可 (Leave)。仅提交上诉通知 (Filing Notice of Appeal) 尚不需要许可。

💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)：
在 MBE 考试中，注意区分 "Filing a Notice of Appeal"（向地区法院提交）和 "Appeal Docketed"（上诉法院立案登记）。

FRCP 60(a) 的分界线是 Docketing。在此之前，地区法院说了算；在此之后，必须先问过“上级”。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A stockbroker was convicted in federal court of criminal fraud in the sale of certain securities. A former client then sued the stockbroker in a federal civil action, alleging fraud in the sale of the same securities for which the stockbroker had been criminally convicted. The client's attorney moved to preclude the stockbroker from relitigating the liability issues that were common to the criminal and civil actions. The court granted the motion and, after a bench trial on damages, entered judgment against the stockbroker for $100,000.
On appeal from the stockbroker's criminal conviction, the appellate court reversed and vacated the conviction. The stockbroker promptly moved for relief from the final judgment in the civil action. The motion was filed 15 months after entry of the final judgment in the civil action.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because it is untimely.
choices.B: No, because the stockbroker did not appeal the civil judgment.
choices.C: Yes, because the court in the civil action should not have based the civil judgment on the criminal judgment before it had been reviewed on appeal.
choices.D: Yes, because the criminal judgment on which the civil judgment was based has been reversed and vacated.

questions.explanation:
Relief from final judgment
(FRCP 60(b))
Grounds for relief Time to file
1. Mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect
2. Newly discovered evidence
3. Fraud, misrepresentation, misconduct 		Within one year
4. Void judgment (eg, lack of jurisdiction)

5. Judgment:
    • satisfied, released, discharged
    • based on reversed or vacated judgment or
    • will violate equity if applied prospectively

6. Other reason justifying relief (rare) 		Within reasonable time

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 60(b) allows a party to move for extraordinary relief from a court's final judgment on limited grounds. The motion must be made within one year from the court's judgment if the motion is based on any of the grounds listed in FRCP 60(b)(1)–(3) (see image above). All other FRCP 60(b) motions can be made within a reasonable time under the circumstances. This includes a motion under FRCP 60(b)(5), which authorizes relief from a judgment that:

  • has been satisfied, released, or discharged
  • is based on an earlier judgment that has been reversed or vacated or
  • will violate equity if applied prospectively.

Here, the federal court granted the client's motion in the civil fraud action to prevent the stockbroker from relitigating the liability issues that had been decided in the stockbroker's criminal fraud action. An appellate court then reversed and vacated the criminal fraud conviction, and the stockbroker promptly moved for relief in the federal civil action pursuant to FRCP 60(b)(5). As a result, the one-year deadline does not apply, and the court should grant the stockbroker's timely motion for relief (Choice A).

(Choice B) A party need not appeal before moving to set aside a judgment under FRCP 60(b). Had the stockbroker appealed the civil judgment, the appeal likely would have been unsuccessful since the court properly applied issue preclusion to prevent the relitigation of identical issues decided in the criminal action.

(Choice C) A final judgment entered in a civil or criminal action is entitled to immediate preclusive effect. This means that the court in the civil action validly based the civil judgment on the criminal judgment before it had been reviewed on appeal.

📌 Educational Objective

Under FRCP 60(b)(5), a party may file a motion within a reasonable time to obtain relief from a judgment that (1) has been satisfied, released, or discharged, (2) is based on an earlier judgment that has been reversed or vacated, or (3) will violate equity if applied prospectively.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 60(b)–(c) (relief from judgment).
  • 11 Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2863 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining that a party may move for relief from a judgment that is based on an earlier judgment that has been reversed or vacated).
questions.zh-question:
一名股票经纪人因在某些证券的销售中犯有刑事欺诈罪，在联邦法院被定罪。随后，一名前客户在联邦民事诉讼中起诉该股票经纪人，指控其在销售与该股票经纪人被刑事定罪的相同证券时存在欺诈行为。该客户的律师动议禁止该股票经纪人就刑事和民事诉讼中共同的责任问题进行再次诉讼。法院批准了该动议，并在对损害赔偿进行法官审理后，作出了不利于该股票经纪人、赔偿10万美元的判决。

在上诉该股票经纪人的刑事定罪时，上诉法院推翻并撤销了该定罪。该股票经纪人立即动议请求从民事诉讼的终局判决中获得救济。该动议在民事诉讼终局判决作出15个月后提出。

法院是否应批准该动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为该动议不合时宜。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为该股票经纪人未对民事判决提起上诉。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为民事诉讼的法院不应在刑事判决经过上诉复核前，将其作为民事判决的基础。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为作为民事判决基础的刑事判决已被推翻并撤销。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Relief from Judgment
正确答案：选项 D
核心考点：FRCP 60(b)(5)

本题考察的是《联邦民事诉讼规则》（Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, FRCP）第60(b)条关于解除终局判决（Relief from Final Judgment）的规定。

FRCP 60(b)(5) 规定： 法院可以解除一方当事人的终局判决，如果该判决是基于一项已被推翻或撤销的先前判决（based on an earlier judgment that has been reversed or vacated）。
案情逻辑分析
刑事定罪 (Judgment A)
股票经纪人因欺诈被定罪。
民事判决 (Judgment B)
基于“争点排除原则”（Issue Preclusion），民事法院直接引用刑事定罪判定经纪人负有民事责任。
刑事定罪被推翻
上诉法院撤销了 Judgment A。
动议救济
经纪人请求撤销基于 Judgment A 作出的 Judgment B。

由于民事判决（Judgment B）的唯一基础是刑事定罪（Judgment A），当基础不复存在时，根据 FRCP 60(b)(5)，法院应当批准解除民事判决。

关键陷阱：时间限制 (Timing)

本题最大的干扰点在于“15个月”。考生需要区分 FRCP 60(b) 中不同理由的时间限制：

理由 时限
(1) 错误/疏忽
(2) 新证据
(3) 欺诈		 绝对不超过1年
(4) 判决无效
(5) 判决基础被推翻
(6) 其他理由		 合理时间内 (Reasonable Time)

虽然民事判决已经过了15个月（超过1年），但本动议是基于 60(b)(5)。规则要求只需在“合理时间内”提出。由于经纪人在刑事判决被推翻后“立即”（promptly）提出了动议，这符合“合理时间”的要求。因此，选项 A（认为不合时宜）是错误的。

其他选项解析
选项 B 错误： 当事人不需要先对民事判决提起上诉才能使用 Rule 60(b)。事实上，如果当时提起上诉，上诉法院也会维持原判，因为当时刑事定罪还是有效的。Rule 60(b) 正是为了处理这种判决后发生变化的情况。
选项 C 错误： 这是一个常见的误区。根据联邦法，未决的上诉（Pending Appeal）并不影响判决的既判力。民事法院在当时完全有权依据尚未被推翻的刑事判决来判定责任。法院当时的做法没有错，只是现在情况变了。
💡 考试技巧：
看到 Rule 60(b) 的题目，首先判断动议的理由是什么。
  • 如果是“发现了新证据”或“律师搞错了”，死记1年红线。
  • 如果是“管辖权缺陷（Void）”或“基础判决被推翻”，则是合理时间。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A plaintiff sued a defendant in federal court for injuries arising out of an accident involving the parties. The plaintiff alleged and presented evidence at trial demonstrating that her injuries had left her legs permanently paralyzed. The jury found in favor of the plaintiff and awarded her $5 million in damages. Two months after the court entered judgment, the defendant was given a video made that day showing the plaintiff jogging with her doctor.
What is the best way for the defendant to seek relief from the judgment?

choices.A: Move for a new trial or in the alternative for remittitur to reduce the award in light of the shortened duration of the plaintiff's injuries.
choices.B: Move for relief from the judgment on the ground that the judgment was based on the jury's mistaken belief that the plaintiff's injuries would be permanent.
choices.C: Move for relief from the judgment on the ground that the plaintiff committed a fraud in obtaining damages for permanent injuries.
choices.D: Move for relief from the judgment on the ground that there is newly discovered evidence that the plaintiff's injuries were not permanent.

questions.explanation:
Relief from final judgment
(FRCP 60(b))
Grounds for relief Time to file
1. Mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect
2. Newly discovered evidence
3. Fraud, misrepresentation, misconduct 		Within one year
4. Void judgment (eg, lack of jurisdiction)
5. Judgment:
    • satisfied, released, discharged
    • based on reversed or vacated judgment or
    • will violate equity if applied prospectively
6. Other reason justifying relief (rare) 		Within reasonable
time
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 60(b), a party can seek extraordinary relief from a district court's final judgment in limited circumstances. This motion may generally be made within a reasonable time, but it must be made within one year from the entry of the final judgment when the motion asserts any of the following grounds for relief:

  • The judgment was due to mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect by the parties or the court (Choice B).
  • The party has discovered new evidence that existed at the time of the trial and could not have reasonably been discovered in time to move for a new trial—ie, within 28 days of the final judgment.
  • The opposing party engaged in misrepresentation, misconduct, or fraud.

Here, the court entered a final judgment awarding the plaintiff $5 million for injuries that allegedly left her legs permanently paralyzed. Two months later, the defendant received a video showing the plaintiff jogging. Since this video shows that the plaintiff committed a fraud in obtaining damages, the defendant should move for relief from the judgment on this ground.

(Choice A) Motions for new trial and motions for remittitur must be filed within 28 days after a final judgment is entered. Since this deadline has passed, the defendant cannot obtain relief through these motions.

(Choice D) Evidence is "newly discovered" if it existed at the time of the trial and could not have reasonably been discovered in time to move for a new trial. Therefore, the video created two months after trial is not newly discovered evidence within the meaning of FRCP 60(b).

📌 Educational Objective

A party may obtain extraordinary relief from a final judgment within one year from the entry of a judgment that is based on (1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect by the parties or court, (2) newly discovered evidence, or (3) the opposing party's fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 60(b)–(c) (extraordinary relief from judgment).
questions.zh-question:
原告因双方之间的一起事故所致的伤害在联邦法院起诉了被告。原告在审判中指称并出示证据，证明其伤害已导致其双腿永久性瘫痪。陪审团作出了有利于原告的裁决，并判给她500万美元的损害赔偿金。在法院作出判决两个月后，被告收到了当天拍摄的一段视频，视频显示原告正在和她的医生一起慢跑。

被告寻求判决救济的最佳方式是什么？

zh-choices.A: 动议进行新的审判，或作为替代方案，动议申请减额赔偿，以根据原告伤害持续时间的缩短来减少赔偿金额。
zh-choices.B: 以判决是基于陪审团错误地认为原告的伤害是永久性的为由，动议寻求判决救济。
zh-choices.C: 以原告在获取永久性伤害的损害赔偿金时实施了欺诈为由，动议寻求判决救济。
zh-choices.D: 以有新发现的证据表明原告的伤害并非永久性为由，动议寻求判决救济。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure (民事诉讼法)
正确答案：C 以原告实施了欺诈 (Fraud) 为由，动议寻求判决救济。
核心考点：FRCP 60(b) 判决救济

本题考察的是《联邦民事诉讼规则》第60(b)条关于解除终局判决 (Relief from a Final Judgment) 的理由和时限。

当判决已经作出且超过了申请“新审判”的期限时，当事人只能寻求“非常救济”。FRCP 60(b) 列出了几种特定理由，其中最相关的包括：

  • (1) 错误、疏忽 (Mistake/Excusable Neglect)
  • (2) 新发现的证据 (Newly Discovered Evidence)
  • (3) 欺诈、虚假陈述 (Fraud/Misrepresentation)

上述三种理由的动议必须在判决作出后 1年内 提出。

⏳ 关键时间线分析
Day 0
法院作出终局判决 (Entry of Judgment)。
Day 28
申请新审判 (New Trial) 或 减额赔偿 (Remittitur) 的截止日期 (FRCP 59)。
2 Months
被告发现视频。此时已超过 FRCP 59 的28天期限，但未超过 FRCP 60(b) 的1年期限。
为什么选 C (Fraud)？

原告在庭审中声称“永久瘫痪”并因此获得巨额赔偿，但判决后仅两个月就能慢跑。这强烈暗示原告在庭审期间对自己的伤情进行了虚假陈述 (Misrepresentation) 或欺诈 (Fraud)。

根据 FRCP 60(b)(3)，如果对方当事人存在欺诈行为，法院可以解除判决。这是最直接符合事实模式的救济途径。

陷阱选项解析
选项 A 错误 (New Trial/Remittitur)：
虽然这通常是处理赔偿过高或证据问题的首选，但 FRCP 59 规定此类动议必须在判决后 28天内 提出。本案已过两个月，时间上被禁止 (Time-barred)。
选项 D 错误 (Newly Discovered Evidence)：
这是一个常见的 MBE 陷阱。FRCP 60(b)(2) 定义的“新发现证据”必须是在审判时已经存在 (existed at the time of trial) 的事实。

题目明确指出视频是“当天拍摄的” (made that day)，即审判后两个月才产生。因此，这个视频本身不是“审判时已存在”的证据。虽然它证明了原告可能在撒谎，但从法律技术上讲，以“欺诈”为由（选项C）比以“新证据”为由更准确、更稳妥。
选项 B 错误 (Mistake)：
虽然陪审团确实“搞错了”原告的伤情，但这种错误是由于原告的欺骗导致的。FRCP 60(b)(1) 的“Mistake”通常指程序性错误或双方的无心之失，而非一方蓄意欺骗的结果。
MBE 解题技巧：
遇到判决后的题目，首先看时间。
≤ 28天 → 优先考虑 Rule 59 (New Trial/JMOL)。
> 28天且 < 1年 → 考虑 Rule 60 (Fraud/New Evidence)。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A woman domiciled in State A was driving in State B when the brakes on her car malfunctioned. As a result, she lost control of her car and hit a concrete traffic barrier. The woman later brought a strict products liability action against the brake manufacturer in a federal court in State A to recover $100,000 in damages. The manufacturer is incorporated and headquartered in State B. The manufacturer conducts no business and has no employees in State A.
The manufacturer filed a motion to dismiss for insufficient service of process, which was denied. The manufacturer has now filed an answer to the woman's complaint and asserted therein a motion to dismiss for improper venue. The woman failed to respond to the motion.
Is the court likely to dismiss the action for improper venue?

choices.A: No, because the manufacturer waived its right to challenge venue.
choices.B: No, unless the court determines that a federal court in State B is a more convenient forum under the doctrine of forum non conveniens.
choices.C: Yes, because the manufacturer resides in State B and the accident occurred there.
choices.D: Yes, because the woman failed to respond to the manufacturer's motion to dismiss.

questions.explanation:
Waiver of defenses
Defenses Waiver
• Lack of subject-matter jurisdiction Never waived
• Lack of personal jurisdiction
• Improper venue
• Insufficient process or service of process 		Waived if not asserted in pre-answer motion or answer (whichever occurs first)
• Failure to state claim
• Failure to join required party 		Waived if not asserted before end of trial
• All other legal defenses Waived if not asserted in answer or amended answer

The following defenses are waived if they are not asserted in a pre-answer motion or answer, whichever occurs first: (1) lack of personal jurisdiction, (2) improper venue, and (3) insufficient process or service of process. Here, the manufacturer filed a pre-answer motion to dismiss for insufficient service of process, but that motion failed to assert the defense of improper venue. The manufacturer therefore waived its right to challenge this issue, and the court is unlikely to dismiss the action for improper venue.

Had the manufacturer preserved its right to challenge venue, the court would have applied the general venue statute to determine if venue is proper in State A. Under this statute, venue is proper in any judicial district where:

  • any defendant resides, so long as all defendants reside in the same state (here, the manufacturer resides in State B)*
  • a substantial part of the events giving rise to the claim occurred or a substantial portion of the property at issue is located (here, the accident occurred in State B) or
  • any defendant is subject to personal jurisdiction, but only if venue cannot be established under either of the above provisions (not applicable here).

Therefore, venue is proper in State B but improper in State A. However, the manufacturer waived its right to challenge venue by failing to do so in its pre-answer motion (Choice C).

*An entity resides in any judicial district where it is subject to personal jurisdiction. As a result, the manufacturer resides in State B because it is incorporated and headquartered there. But it does not reside in State A because it conducts no business and has no employees there.

(Choice B) The doctrine of forum non conveniens allows a federal court to dismiss or stay a case if a state or foreign judicial system, not another federal court, is better suited to hear the dispute.

(Choice D) The woman had no duty to respond to the manufacturer's answer containing the motion to dismiss for improper venue. That is because a plaintiff need only respond to a defendant's answer if the defendant asserted a counterclaim or the court orders a reply (neither seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The defenses of (1) lack of personal jurisdiction, (2) improper venue, and (3) insufficient process or service of process are waived if they are not asserted in a pre-answer motion or answer, whichever occurs first.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(h) (waiver of defenses).
questions.zh-question:
一名居住在A州的女性在B州驾车时，其汽车刹车失灵。结果，她对车辆失去控制，撞上了混凝土交通护栏。该女性随后在A州的联邦法院对刹车制造商提起了严格产品责任诉讼，要求10万美元的损害赔偿。该制造商在B州注册成立，总部也设在B州。该制造商在A州没有开展任何业务，也没有任何雇员。

制造商以送达程序不充分为由提交了驳回动议，但该动议被驳回。现在，制造商已对该女性的诉状提交了答辩状，并在其中主张了以审判地不当为由的驳回动议。该女性未对该动议作出回应。

法院是否可能以审判地不当为由驳回该诉讼？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为制造商放弃了其对审判地提出异议的权利。
zh-choices.B: 否，除非法院根据“不方便法院原则”(forum non conveniens) 认定B州的联邦法院是更便利的审理法院。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为制造商居住在B州，且事故也发生在该州。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该女性未对制造商的驳回动议作出回应。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Motions & Waiver
正确答案：A

法院不会驳回诉讼，因为制造商已经放弃 (Waived) 了对审判地 (Venue) 提出异议的权利。

核心考点：FRCP 12(h) 抗辩的放弃

根据《联邦民事诉讼规则》(Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, FRCP) 第 12 条，被告必须在第一次回应（无论是答辩前动议还是答辩状）中一次性提出某些特定的程序性抗辩。这被称为"Use it or lose it"（要么使用，要么失效）规则。

⚠️ 必须在第一次回应中提出的抗辩：
  • Rule 12(b)(2) 缺乏属人管辖权 (Lack of Personal Jurisdiction)
  • Rule 12(b)(3) 审判地不当 (Improper Venue)
  • Rule 12(b)(4) 诉讼程序不充分 (Insufficient Process)
  • Rule 12(b)(5) 送达程序不充分 (Insufficient Service of Process)

如果被告选择提交一个答辩前动议 (Pre-answer Motion)，他必须将上述所有已知的抗辩理由都包含在这一份动议中。如果遗漏了其中任何一项，该项抗辩即被视为放弃 (Waived)，之后不能在答辩状 (Answer) 或后续动议中再次提出。

本案逻辑分析
1
第一次行动：
制造商提交了答辩前动议，理由是“送达程序不充分”。
2
关键错误：
在这次动议中，制造商没有包含“审判地不当”这一抗辩理由。
3
法律后果：
根据 FRCP 12(g) 和 12(h)(1)，制造商已经永久放弃了挑战审判地的权利。
4
后续无效：
虽然制造商后来在答辩状 (Answer) 中写进了审判地异议，但为时已晚，该权利已经灭失。
为什么其他选项是错的？
  • 选项 C (错误)： 虽然从事实看，A 州确实可能不是正确的审判地（事故在 B 州，被告在 B 州），但程序性放弃 (Waiver) 优先于实体事实。一旦权利被放弃，法院就不再审查审判地是否实际上正确。
  • 选项 B (错误)： Forum non conveniens（不方便法院原则）通常用于审判地本身是适当的，但另一个司法管辖区（通常是外国或州法院）更合适的情况。本题的核心考点是 Rule 12 的放弃规则，而非方便原则。
  • 选项 D (错误)： 原告通常不需要对被告的答辩状 (Answer) 做出回应，除非法院下令或被告提出了反诉 (Counterclaim)。原告的沉默不代表认同。
💡 MBE 提分技巧：
看到被告提交了 Motion to Dismiss，立即检查他是否遗漏了 PJ (管辖权)、Venue (审判地) 或 Service (送达)。如果第一次动议里没写，第二次就不能再提了！记住："One Shot Rule"（一次机会规则）。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A store owner from State A had a dispute with its supplier incorporated and headquartered in State B over the quality of the produce the supplier had delivered to the store. The store owner sued the supplier in a federal court in State A for breach of contract, seeking $200,000 in damages.
The supplier filed a pre-answer motion to dismiss the case based solely on lack of personal jurisdiction, which the court denied. The supplier now seeks to assert that the federal court is an improper venue and that the store owner failed to state a claim on which relief can be granted.
Which of the following statements best describes the effect of the supplier's pre-answer motion on these two defenses?

choices.A: It has no effect on the supplier's "improper venue" or "failure to state a claim" defense.
choices.B: It resulted in a waiver of the supplier's "failure to state a claim" defense.
choices.C: It resulted in a waiver of the supplier's "improper venue" defense.
choices.D: It resulted in a waiver of the supplier's "improper venue" and "failure to state a claim" defenses.

questions.explanation:
Omnibus motion rule
FRCP 12 defenses
Effect if omitted from pre-answer motion
  • Lack of personal jurisdiction
  • Improper venue
  • Insufficient process/service of process
→
  • Subsequent pre-answer motion prohibited
  • Defenses waived
  • Failure to state claim on which to grant relief
  • Failure to state legal defense
  • Failure to join required party
→
  • Subsequent pre-answer motion prohibited
  • Defenses not waived at trial
  • Lack of subject-matter jurisdiction
→
  • Subsequent pre-answer motion allowed
  • Defense never waived

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A defendant must respond to a plaintiff's complaint by filing an answer or a pre-answer motion. When the defendant files a pre-answer motion, the omnibus motion rule requires that all FRCP 12 defenses be consolidated in a single motion for efficiency purposes. This means that the defendant cannot file a subsequent pre-answer motion raising an omitted FRCP 12 defense—except for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction*—that was available when the initial motion was filed.

Because of the omnibus motion rule, the following FRCP 12 defenses are waived and cannot be asserted later if omitted from a pre-answer motion: (1) lack of personal jurisdiction, (2) improper venue, and (3) insufficient process or service of process. Here, the supplier's pre-answer motion failed to include the "improper venue" defense, so this defense was waived (Choice A).

However, the following FRCP 12 defenses may still be later asserted in an answer or post-answer motion if omitted from a pre-answer motion: (1) failure to state a claim, (2) failure to state a legal defense, and (3) failure to join a required party. As a result, the supplier's omission of its "failure to state a claim" defense from the pre-answer motion did not waive this defense. It may still be asserted in the supplier's answer or in a post-answer motion (Choices B & D).

*Lack of subject-matter jurisdiction is never waived and may be asserted at any time, including in a subsequent pre-answer motion.

📌 Educational Objective

The omnibus motion rule requires that all FRCP 12 defenses be consolidated in a single pre-answer motion. Lack of personal jurisdiction, improper venue, and insufficient process or service of process are waived if omitted. But failure to state a claim, state a legal defense, or join a required party may still be asserted in an answer or post-answer motion.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(g)–(h) (consolidating and waiving pre-answer defenses).
  • 5C Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 1385 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining the omnibus motion rule).
questions.zh-question:
一名来自 A 州的店主，与其在 B 州注册成立且总部设在 B 州的供应商，就供应商向该店交付的农产品质量发生争议。店主以违约为由在 A 州的联邦法院起诉该供应商，要求赔偿 20 万美元的损失。

供应商提交了一份答辩前动议，以缺乏对人管辖权为唯一理由请求驳回此案，但该动议被法院驳回。现在，供应商试图主张该联邦法院是不当审判地，并且店主未能陈述可据以准予救济的诉求。

以下哪项陈述最准确地描述了供应商的答辩前动议对这两项抗辩理由的影响？

zh-choices.A: 该动议对供应商的“不当审判地”或“未能陈述诉求”的抗辩理由没有影响。
zh-choices.B: 该动议导致供应商放弃了“未能陈述诉求”的抗辩理由。
zh-choices.C: 该动议导致供应商放弃了“不当审判地”的抗辩理由。
zh-choices.D: 该动议导致供应商放弃了“不当审判地”和“未能陈述诉求”的抗辩理由。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Rule 12 Defenses

正确答案：C 该动议导致供应商放弃了“不当审判地”的抗辩理由，但并未放弃“未能陈述诉求”的抗辩。
⚖️ 核心考点：Omnibus Motion Rule

本题考查《联邦民事诉讼规则》(FRCP) 第 12 条关于抗辩理由的合并与放弃（Consolidation and Waiver of Defenses）。

规则核心 (Rule 12(g) & 12(h)):
如果你选择提交答辩前动议（Pre-answer Motion），你必须将所有当时可用的 Rule 12 抗辩理由一次性合并在该动议中。

根据这一规则，抗辩理由被分为三类，其后果截然不同：

抗辩类型 后果 (若遗漏)
第一类：严格放弃
1. 对人管辖权 (PJ)
2. 审判地 (Venue)
3. 送达/文书瑕疵 		永久放弃 (Waived)。
如果在第一次动议中未提出，以后再也不能提出了。
第二类：保留
1. 未能陈述诉求 (Failure to state a claim)
2. 未能加入必要方 		不放弃 (Not Waived)。
虽然不能再发第二个答辩前动议，但可以在答辩状 (Answer) 或审判 (Trial) 中提出。
第三类：永不放弃
事物管辖权 (SMJ) 		随时提出。
甚至可以在上诉阶段提出。
🔍 案情具体分析

在本案中，供应商（被告）提交了第一个答辩前动议，仅主张了“缺乏对人管辖权”。

  1. 关于“不当审判地” (Improper Venue)：
    属于第一类抗辩。因为被告在第一次动议中遗漏了它，根据 Rule 12(h)(1)，该抗辩被永久放弃。
  2. 关于“未能陈述诉求” (Failure to state a claim)：
    属于第二类抗辩。根据 Rule 12(h)(2)，虽然被告不能为此再单独发一个 Rule 12(b) 动议（因为 Rule 12(g) 禁止拆分动议），但这并不意味着他放弃了这个抗辩。他仍然可以在后续的答辩状 (Answer) 中提出。

因此，只有“不当审判地”被放弃了，选 C。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
  • 选项 A： 错误。它认为两个抗辩都没受影响，但实际上“不当审判地”已经被放弃了。
  • 选项 B & D： 错误。它们认为“未能陈述诉求”被放弃了。这是 MBE 常见的陷阱——虽然你不能发第二个动议来提它，但你并没有“放弃”这个法律理由本身，你只是换个时间（在 Answer 中）提出来。
💡 MBE 提分技巧 在做 Civil Procedure 题目时，一旦看到被告提交了 Pre-answer Motion，立刻警惕：
1. 检查他漏掉了什么。
2. 漏掉的是不是 "Waivable Defenses" (PJ, Venue, Process, Service)。
3. 如果是，那就是 Waived；如果是 12(b)(6) (Failure to state a claim)，则只是推迟提出 (Preserved)。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A plaintiff sued a defendant in federal court for trademark infringement. At the conclusion of trial, the judge instructed the 10-member jury. In the jury deliberation room, one of the jurors pulled out his cell phone and searched for "trademark infringement." He read aloud from an article that said, "trademark infringement hurts the U.S. economy." The jury foreman directed the juror to stop reading and sent a note to the judge describing the incident.
The judge brought the jury back to the courtroom and reminded the members of their obligation not to consult outside sources during deliberations. She confiscated their phones, instructed them to ignore the juror's misconduct, and directed them to continue deliberating. The jury returned to the deliberation room. After three hours, the jury returned a verdict in favor of the defendant. The court entered a final judgment consistent with the verdict.
The plaintiff moved for a new trial based on the juror's conduct 21 days after the entry of the final judgment.
How will the judge likely rule on the plaintiff's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the juror's misconduct was harmless.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the plaintiff waived its right to challenge the juror's conduct by filing an untimely motion for new trial.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the judge should have removed the juror from the jury.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the juror engaged in misconduct by consulting outside information.

questions.explanation:
Grounds for new trial
  • Prejudicial trial error (eg, erroneous evidentiary ruling)
  • Prejudicial misconduct by judge, attorney, party, or juror
  • Verdict not supported by clear weight of evidence
  • Verdict based on false/nonexistent evidence
  • Excessive or inadequate damages
  • Newly discovered evidence

A court can grant a new trial if a juror (or judge, party, or attorney) engaged in prejudicial misconduct during the trial. Misconduct is prejudicial when it affects a party's substantial rights. This requires the court to determine with fair assurance whether the jury's verdict was influenced by the misconduct. If there was no improper influence, then the misconduct was harmless and does not provide a basis for a new trial. For example, misconduct can be made harmless (ie, "cured") if the judge admonishes the jury to disregard that conduct.

Here, a juror read aloud from an article that "trademark infringement hurts the U.S. economy." This misconduct may have initially prejudiced the defendant who had allegedly engaged in trademark infringement. But it did not prejudice the plaintiff because the statement supported the plaintiff as the holder of the trademark.* Therefore, the court will likely find that the misconduct was harmless and deny the plaintiff's motion for a new trial (Choice A).

*Even if this misconduct had prejudiced the plaintiff, the prejudice was likely cured when the judge confiscated the jurors' phones, instructed them to ignore the juror's misconduct, and directed them to continue deliberating.

(Choice B) A party must file a motion for a new trial within 28 days after the entry of a final judgment. Therefore, the plaintiff's motion for new trial—filed 21 days after the court entered the final judgment—was timely.

(Choice C) A juror may be removed during trial if the juror can no longer capably serve on the jury (eg, due to medical issues) or if the juror engaged in misconduct (as seen here). However, the judge has considerable discretion to decide whether removal is warranted.

📌 Educational Objective

A new trial is warranted when a juror engaged in prejudicial misconduct—ie, misconduct that affects a party's substantial rights by influencing the jury's verdict. If misconduct is not prejudicial, then it is merely harmless error that does not warrant a new trial.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 61 (harmless error).
  • 58 Am. Jur. 2d New Trial § 143 (2019) (explaining that a juror's misconduct must be prejudicial to warrant a new trial).
questions.zh-question:
原告在联邦法院就商标侵权起诉被告。庭审结束时，法官对由10名成员组成的陪审团进行了指示。在陪审团评议室，一名陪审员拿出手机搜索了“商标侵权”。他朗读了一篇文章，文中称“商标侵权损害美国经济”。陪审团主席指示该陪审员停止朗读，并向法官递交了一张描述该事件的便条。

法官将陪审团带回法庭，并提醒其成员在评议期间有义务不查阅外部信息来源。她没收了他们的手机，指示他们忽略该陪审员的不当行为，并命令他们继续评议。陪审团回到评议室。三小时后，陪审团作出了有利于被告的裁决。法院根据该裁决作出了最终判决。

在最终判决作出21天后，原告以该陪审员的行为为由，申请进行新的审判。

法官可能会如何裁定原告的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为陪审员的不当行为是无害的。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为原告因未及时提交新审判的动议而放弃了挑战陪审员行为的权利。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为法官本应将该陪审员从陪审团中除名。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为陪审员查阅外部信息构成了不当行为。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: New Trial & Juror Misconduct

正确答案：A
(驳回动议，因为不当行为是无害的)
核心考点：无害错误原则

在联邦民事诉讼规则（FRCP 61）下，并非所有的错误都会导致新的审判（New Trial）。

只有当错误或不当行为是具有偏见性的（Prejudicial），即影响了当事人的实质性权利（Substantial Rights）时，法院才会批准重审。

如果错误没有影响案件结果，或者对败诉方没有造成不公，这被称为无害错误（Harmless Error）。

本案逻辑推演

1. 识别不当行为：
陪审员确实进行了不当行为（上网搜索并朗读文章），这违反了陪审团指令。

2. 分析内容倾向：
陪审员朗读的内容是：“商标侵权损害美国经济”。
👉 这句话本质上是反对侵权的，倾向于保护商标持有者（即本案的原告）。

3. 判定偏见归属：
虽然有不当行为，但该外部信息实际上是在帮助原告。然而，陪审团最终还是判决被告胜诉。

结论： 原告不能声称这个“有利于自己”的外部信息导致了自己败诉。因此，该不当行为对原告没有造成实质性损害（Prejudice）。

4. 法官的补救措施：
法官及时没收了手机并给出了补救指示（Curative Instruction），要求陪审团忽略该行为。法律通常假定陪审团会遵守法官的指示。

干扰项排除
❌ 选项 B (时效问题)：
根据 FRCP 59(b)，新审判动议必须在判决录入后 28天 内提出。本案中原告在 21 天时提出，完全在时效内，并未放弃权利。
❌ 选项 C (除名问题)：
虽然法官可以将陪审员除名，但这属于法官的自由裁量权。未除名并不自动构成重审理由，关键还是看是否造成了偏见。
❌ 选项 D (仅凭不当行为)：
这是最大的陷阱。仅仅证明有“不当行为”（Misconduct）是不够的，必须证明该行为产生了“偏见”（Prejudice）。没有偏见的不当行为是无害的。
💡 MBE 考试技巧：
在处理“程序错误”或“不当行为”的题目时，不要看到错误就直接选“重审”或“撤销判决”。

一定要多问一步：“谁受了伤？” (Who was hurt?)
如果提出动议的一方并没有因为该错误受到不公正的待遇（或者该错误其实是有利于他们的），那么这就是Harmless Error，动议会被驳回。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An employee sued her employer for violation of the Americans with Disabilities Act. At trial there was a dispute over whether the employee's supervisor told her in a conversation that she was being dismissed because of her Tourette's syndrome. The jury found for the employee and awarded her damages. Six months after the entry of the judgment in this case, the employer learned that the employee, without her supervisor's knowledge, had recorded the conversation in question. Obtaining a copy of the recording, the employer learned that the employee had lied about the content of the conversation.
Which of the following motions with respect to this judgment can the employer now make to the district court?

choices.A: A motion for relief from the judgment under Rule 60(b).
choices.B: A motion to alter or amend the judgment under Rule 59(e).
choices.C: A motion to correct the judgment under Rule 60(a).
choices.D: A motion to set aside the judgment for fraud on the court under Rule 60(d).

questions.explanation:
Relief from final judgment
(FRCP 60(b))
Grounds for relief Time to file
1. Mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect
2. Newly discovered evidence
3. Fraud, misrepresentation, misconduct 		Within one year
4. Void judgment (eg, lack of jurisdiction)
5. Judgment:
   • satisfied, released, discharged
   • based on reversed or vacated judgment or
   • will violate equity if applied prospectively
6. Other reason justifying relief (rare) 		Within reasonable
time
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

FRCP 60(b) allows a party to move for relief from a final judgment on limited grounds. The deadline to file such a motion depends on the reason that relief is sought. When the motion is based on one of the following grounds, it must be filed within a reasonable time, but no later than one year after entry of the judgment:

  • mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect
  • newly discovered evidence that could not have been discovered earlier with reasonable diligence or
  • fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct by an opposing party.

Here, a final judgment was entered in the employee's favor. Six months later, the employer discovered that the employee had lied during trial about the content of a conversation with her supervisor. This constitutes fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct by an opposing party—a proper basis for a motion for relief from a judgment.* And since the judgment was entered less than a year ago, such motion would not be inherently untimely. Therefore, the employer can now make a motion for relief from the judgment under Rule 60(b) to the district court.

*Alternatively, the employer could base its motion on the newly discovered recording of the conversation between the employee and her supervisor. But since no facts indicate that the recording could not have been discovered earlier with reasonable diligence, the employee's act of lying during trial is likely a stronger basis for the motion.

(Choice B) A motion to alter or amend a judgment under Rule 59(e) must be made within 28 days of the judgment's entry. Because six months have passed here, this motion is unavailable.

(Choice C) A motion to correct a judgment under Rule 60(a) asks the court to correct a mistake that occurred due to an oversight or omission (not seen here).

(Choice D) Rule 60(d) allows a court to set aside a judgment at any time for fraud on the court. "Fraud on the court" is fraud that seriously affects the integrity of the judicial process (e.g., bribing a judge). The employee's conduct here does not rise to the level of fraud on the court.

📌 Educational Objective

A motion for relief from judgment under Rule 60(b) may be brought based on fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct by an opposing party. The motion must be made within a reasonable time, but no later than one year after entry of the judgment.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 60 (relief from a judgment or order).

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.topic: Alteration of or Relief of a Judgment
questions.question:
A state opened a new park near a residential neighborhood. One of the residents sued the state in federal district court, claiming that the state took some of his property for the new park without providing him just compensation.
At trial, the resident entered an old, unrecorded document into evidence that supported his claim that he owned the disputed property. In its defense, the state entered hundreds of documents into evidence that showed that the disputed property was state-owned land. At the end of trial, the jury returned a verdict in favor of the state, and the court entered a final judgment consistent with the verdict.
The next day, the resident hired a professional researcher to meticulously search the state and county records relating to the property. The researcher discovered a misfiled document in the county records that conclusively showed that the resident, not the state, owned the disputed property. This document was not entered into evidence at trial. The resident immediately moved for a new trial based on this newly discovered evidence.
Is the court likely to grant the resident's motion for a new trial?

choices.A: No, because the resident could have discovered the document before the end of trial had he exercised due diligence.
choices.B: No, because the resident must present the document on appeal.
choices.C: Yes, because the document is material to the resident's case.
choices.D: Yes, because the document will likely produce a different result at a new trial.

questions.explanation:
Grounds for new trial
  • Prejudicial trial error (eg, erroneous evidentiary ruling)
  • Prejudicial misconduct by judge, attorney, party, or juror
  • Verdict not supported by clear weight of evidence
  • Verdict based on false/nonexistent evidence
  • Excessive or inadequate damages
  • Newly discovered evidence

Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 59 allows a party to move for a new trial after the entry of a final judgment on certain grounds, including when new evidence is discovered after trial. A court will grant a new trial based on newly discovered evidence if the movant shows that:

• the evidence was unknown to the movant at the time of trial
• the movant used due diligence to discover the evidence before the end of trial
• the evidence is material—not cumulative or impeaching—and
• a new trial considering the evidence will likely result in a different outcome.

Here, the researcher discovered a document after trial that had not been entered into evidence. This document conclusively shows that the resident owns the disputed property, so it is material to his case and would likely lead to a different result at a new trial. However, the resident did not use due diligence to discover the document because he could have hired the researcher or conducted his own search before the end of trial. As a result, the court will likely deny the resident's motion for a new trial on this ground (Choices C & D).

(Choice B) When an appellate court reviews a decision by a lower court, it is limited to the facts and evidence contained in the record. Therefore, the resident cannot present the document for the first time on appeal.

📌 Educational Objective

A court will grant a motion for a new trial based on newly discovered evidence if the movant shows that (1) the evidence was unknown to the movant at trial, (2) due diligence was used to discover the evidence before trial ended, (3) the evidence is material, and (4) a new trial with the evidence will likely have a different outcome.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 59(a) (new trial).
  • 58 Am. Jur. 2d New Trial § 291 (2019) (explaining the requirements for a new trial based on newly discovered evidence).
questions.zh-question:
某州在一个居民区附近开设了一个新公园。一位居民在联邦地区法院起诉该州，声称该州为建设新公园占用了他的部分财产，但未提供公正的补偿。

在审判中，该居民提交了一份未作记录的旧文件作为证据，以支持其对争议财产的所有权主张。作为辩护，该州提交了数百份文件作为证据，表明争议财产是州有土地。审判结束时，陪审团作出了有利于该州的裁决，法院根据该裁决作出了终审判决。

第二天，该居民聘请了一位专业研究员，仔细搜查与该财产相关的州和县的记录。该研究员在县记录中发现了一份被错误归档的文件，该文件确凿地表明，争议财产的所有人是该居民，而不是该州。这份文件在审判中并未被提交为证据。该居民立即根据这一新发现的证据申请重审。

法院是否可能批准该居民的重审申请？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为如果该居民尽到了应有的注意义务，他本可以在审判结束前发现该文件。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该居民必须在上诉中提交该文件。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该文件对该居民的案件至关重要。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该文件很可能在重审中产生不同的结果。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Motion for New Trial
正确答案：A

本题考察的核心知识点是《联邦民事诉讼规则》第59条（FRCP 59）下，基于"新发现的证据" (Newly Discovered Evidence) 申请重审的严格标准。

⚖️ 法律规则 (The Rule)

要基于新发现的证据成功申请重审，申请人必须证明以下所有要素：

  • 时间性：该证据在审判结束前是未知的。
  • 尽职调查 (Due Diligence)：申请人在审判结束前已尽到了应有的注意义务去寻找该证据，但仍未发现。
  • 重要性 (Materiality)：该证据不是累积性的 (Cumulative) 或仅用于弹劾 (Impeaching)。
  • 结果导向：如果采纳该证据，很可能会改变审判结果。

🔍 案情深度解析

在本案中，虽然这份"错误归档的文件" (Misfiled Document) 确实非常关键（Material），并且足以改变判决结果（Would change the outcome），但申请人倒在了"尽职调查" (Due Diligence) 这一关。

关键事实：

  • 该文件存在于公共记录（县记录）中。
  • 居民是在审判失败后才聘请专业研究员去搜查的。

法律逻辑：

法院通常认为，公共记录中的文件是可以被发现的。如果居民在审判前就像审判后那样聘请研究员，他本可以发现这份文件。因为他没有在审判前采取这一行动，法律认定他未尽到应有的注意义务。

因此，尽管证据很有力，法院也会驳回重审申请，以维护判决的终局性 (Finality of Judgments)。

选项 B 错误
上诉法院不接受新证据。
上诉审查仅限于初审法院的案卷记录 (Record)。如果证据未在初审中提交，上诉法院通常不会考虑。
选项 C & D 错误
只看结果，忽略了前提。
这两个选项正确地指出了证据的重要性（Materiality）和对结果的影响，但忽略了必须满足"尽职调查"这一先决条件。如果未能证明尽职调查，证据再重要也无法作为重审理由。
💡 MBE 考试技巧：
看到 "Newly Discovered Evidence" 时，第一反应要检查当事人是否偷懒了 (Lack of Due Diligence)。如果是公共记录里的东西，通常都被视为本应在审判前发现的。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.topic: Judgment as a matter of law
questions.question:
A customer sued a retailer in federal court, claiming that the retailer had intentionally engaged in trade practices that violated federal law. At the close of evidence, the retailer filed a motion for judgment as a matter of law, which was denied. The jury returned a verdict for the customer.
Twenty-five days after the court entered judgment on the verdict, the retailer filed a renewed motion for judgment as a matter of law. The trial court determined that the evidence was legally insufficient to find in the customer's favor because the customer's main witness was not credible. The trial court then issued an order granting the retailer's motion. Twenty-eight days later, the customer appealed.
Is the appellate court likely to uphold the trial court's ruling?

choices.A: No, because the retailer renewed its motion for judgment as a matter of law more than 21 days after the trial court entered judgment on the verdict.
choices.B: No, because the trial court considered the credibility of the customer's main witness when granting the retailer's renewed motion.
choices.C: Yes, because the appellate court must give great deference to the trial court's ruling.
choices.D: Yes, because the customer appealed more than 30 days after the trial court entered judgment on the verdict.

questions.explanation:
Motion for judgment as a matter of law
(FRCP 50)
Time to file
  • May be filed after nonmovant presents its case but before case is submitted to jury (i.e., motion for a directed verdict)
  • May be renewed within 28 days after entry of final judgment (i.e., motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict)
Procedural requirements
  • Movant must:
    • specify judgment sought & law/facts entitling movant to judgment
  • Court must:
    • view evidence & draw all reasonable inferences in nonmovant's favor
    • disregard evidence favorable to movant that a jury is not required to believe
    • not consider credibility of witnesses or evaluate weight of evidence
Standard for grant Evidence is legally insufficient for reasonable jury to find in nonmovant's favor

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A motion for judgment as a matter of law (JMOL) is a request that the court enter a judgment in favor of the movant because the evidence is legally insufficient for a reasonable jury to find in the nonmovant's favor. An initial motion for JMOL must be filed before the case is submitted to the jury. If that motion is denied, the movant can file a renewed motion within 28 days after the entry of final judgment on the jury's verdict.*

When considering an initial or renewed motion for JMOL, the trial court must:

  • view the evidence and draw all reasonable inferences in the light most favorable to the nonmovant
  • disregard any evidence favorable to the movant that the jury is not required to believe and
  • not consider the credibility of witnesses or evaluate the weight of evidence.

Here, the retailer timely renewed its motion for JMOL 25 days after the trial court entered judgment on the jury's verdict (Choice A). The trial court granted this motion after determining that the evidence was legally insufficient to find in the customer's favor. However, the appellate court will likely overturn that ruling because the trial court improperly considered the credibility of the customer's main witness.

*A trial court can grant the renewed motion even if the initial motion was denied. This is often done so that the jury's verdict can be reinstated if the trial court's decision is overturned on appeal.

(Choice C) A trial court's discretionary rulings (eg, admissibility of evidence) are reviewed for abuse of discretion and are given great deference. However, a trial court's legal rulings (eg, granting or denying JMOL) are reviewed de novo and are given no deference.

(Choice D) A notice of appeal must be filed within 30 days after entry of a final judgment or an order disposing of a posttrial motion. Therefore, the customer timely appealed 28 days after the trial court entered a posttrial order granting the renewed motion for JMOL.

📌 Educational Objective

When considering a motion for JMOL, a court must (1) view the evidence and draw all reasonable inferences in favor of the nonmovant, (2) disregard evidence favorable to the movant that the jury is not required to believe, and (3) not consider the credibility of witnesses or evaluate the weight of evidence.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(a) (motion for judgment as a matter of law).
  • Reeves v. Sanderson Plumbing Prods., Inc., 530 U.S. 133, 150–51 (2000) (explaining the procedural requirements for considering a JMOL motion).
questions.zh-question:
一位顾客在联邦法院起诉了一家零售商，声称该零售商故意从事了违反联邦法律的贸易行为。在证据调查结束时，零售商提出了法律上判决的动议（judgment as a matter of law），但该动议被驳回。陪审团作出了有利于顾客的裁决。

在法院根据该裁决作出判决后的第二十五天，零售商提交了一份更新的法律上判决的动议（renewed motion for judgment as a matter of law）。初审法院认定，由于顾客的主要证人不可信，证据在法律上不足以支持有利于顾客的裁决。初审法院随后发布命令，批准了零售商的动议。二十八天后，顾客提起了上诉。

上诉法院是否可能维持初审法院的裁定？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为零售商在初审法院根据裁决作出判决后超过21天才更新其法律上判决的动议。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为初审法院考量了顾客主要证人的可信度。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为顾客在初审法院根据裁决作出判决后超过30天才提起上诉。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为初审法院认定证据在法律上不足以支持有利于顾客的裁决。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: JMOL Standards
正确答案：B 上诉法院不会维持初审法院的裁定，因为初审法院错误地考量了顾客主要证人的可信度 (Credibility)。
核心考点：JMOL 的审查标准

本题考察的是《联邦民事诉讼规则》第50条 (FRCP 50) 关于法律判决动议 (Judgment as a Matter of Law, JMOL) 的核心原则。

规则要点：
在审理 JMOL（无论是初次还是更新后的 Renewed JMOL）时，法官必须：
  • 以对非动议方最有利 (Light most favorable to the nonmovant) 的角度审视证据。
  • 禁止衡量证据的权重 (Weigh the evidence)。
  • 禁止评估证人的可信度 (Determine witness credibility)。

逻辑分析：
在本案中，初审法院批准零售商动议的理由是“顾客的主要证人不可信 (not credible)”。

这是严重的法律错误。
在美国民事诉讼中，可信度是陪审团 (Jury) 专属的判断领域。法官不能因为自己不相信某个证人就推翻陪审团的裁决。只要该证词在法律上能支持裁决，法官就必须接受陪审团相信该证人的选择。

为什么其他选项是错误的？

本题还考察了诉讼时效 (Timing) 的计算，这是 MBE 的常见陷阱。

判决录入 (Entry of Judgment)
陪审团裁决有利于顾客。
第 25 天
零售商提交 Renewed JMOL。
✔ 及时 (期限为28天)
法院裁定
法院批准 JMOL，推翻陪审团裁决。
裁定后第 28 天
顾客提起上诉。
✔ 及时 (期限为30天)
  • 选项 A 错误： Renewed JMOL 的期限是判决录入后的 28天 内 (FRCP 50(b))。零售商在第25天提交，完全合规。
  • 选项 C 错误： 上诉通知 (Notice of Appeal) 的期限通常是判决后的30天。但是，如果有及时的审后动议 (如 Renewed JMOL)，上诉期限会重新计算，从法院处置该动议的命令录入之日起算 30天 (FRCP 4(a)(4))。顾客在动议裁决后28天提起上诉，是及时的。
  • 选项 D 错误： 虽然法院确实认定证据“法律上不足”，但其认定的基础（证人可信度）是非法的。因此上诉法院不会维持该裁定。
MBE 考试技巧

在遇到涉及 JMOL 或 Summary Judgment (简易判决) 的题目时，请寻找以下关键词作为“红旗”：

  • "Credibility" (可信度)
  • "Weighing evidence" (衡量证据)
  • "Believed the witness" (相信证人)

一旦法官在这些动议阶段做了上述行为，通常都是可逆转的错误 (Reversible Error)，因为法官侵犯了陪审团作为事实认定者 (Fact-finder) 的职能。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.topic: Alteration of or Relief of a Judgment
questions.question:
A car manufacturer sued one of its competitors for infringing the manufacturer's patented technology for its self-driving cars. During discovery, the manufacturer requested that the competitor produce all documents related to the competitor's research into self-driving technology. The competitor turned over millions of documents, none of which contained any information related to the manufacturer's patented technology.
The case proceeded to trial, and the jury returned a verdict in favor of the competitor. Six months after the court entered a judgment consistent with this verdict, the competitor's CEO was charged with criminal negligence after several of the competitor's self-driving cars caused accidents. During a search of the competitor's research labs, the police discovered several documents containing information about the manufacturer's patented self-driving technology. The documents had been saved to the competitor's computers three years earlier.
What action may the manufacturer take upon discovering this new evidence?

choices.A: Move for a new trial.
choices.B: Move for judgment as a matter of law.
choices.C: Move for relief from the prior judgment.
choices.D: Move for summary judgment.

questions.explanation:
Posttrial relief
Relief Grounds Timing
Attorney's fees • Statute or rule allows recovery ≤ 14 days after entry of final judgment
Judgment as a matter of law • Evidence legally insufficient to find for nonmovant ≤ 28 days after entry of final judgment
New trial • Prejudicial trial error
• Prejudicial misconduct by judge, attorney, party, juror
• Verdict not supported by clear weight of evidence
• Verdict based on false/nonexistent evidence
• Excessive or inadequate damages
• Newly discovered evidence
Alter/amend judgment • Manifest error of law or fact is basis for judgment
• Intervening change in controlling law
• Newly discovered evidence
Correction of mistake • Clerical mistake
• Mistake arising from oversight or omission 		Freely OR with appellate court's leave if docketed
Extraordinary relief • Mistake, inadvertence, surprise, excusable neglect
• Newly discovered evidence
• Fraud, misrepresentation, misconduct by opposing party 		≤ 1 year after entry of final judgment
• Void judgment
• Judgment satisfied, released, discharged
• Other reason justifying relief 		Within reasonable time

Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60(b) allows a party to move for extraordinary relief from a final judgment or court order on limited grounds. This motion may generally be made within a reasonable time, but it must be made within one year from the entry of a final judgment or order when based on any of the following grounds:

  • The judgment was due to mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect by the parties or the court.
  • The moving party discovered new evidence that (1) existed at the time of the trial and (2) could not have reasonably been discovered in time to move for a new trial (ie, within 28 days of the entry of final judgment).
  • The opposing party engaged in fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct.

Here, the competitor engaged in misconduct during discovery when it failed to disclose the documents containing information about the manufacturer's patented technology. This newly discovered evidence existed at the time of trial but could not have reasonably been discovered until now. And since only six months have passed since the court entered a final judgment, the manufacturer can move for relief from this prior judgment.

(Choice A) A motion for a new trial must be filed within 28 days after the final judgment is entered. Therefore, this motion would be untimely and likely denied.

(Choice B) A party can renew a motion for judgment as a matter of law (JMOL) within 28 days after the court enters final judgment as long as that party moved for JMOL before the case was submitted to the jury.

(Choice D) A motion for summary judgment must be filed within 30 days after the end of discovery (ie, before trial).

📌 Educational Objective

A party can move for extraordinary relief within one year from the entry of a final judgment or court order that is based on (1) mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or excusable neglect, (2) newly discovered evidence, or (3) the opposing party's fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 60(b)–(c) (extraordinary relief from judgment).
questions.zh-question:
一家汽车制造商起诉其竞争对手，称其侵犯了该制造商的自动驾驶汽车专利技术。在证据开示（discovery）程序中，该制造商要求竞争对手出示所有与竞争对手自动驾驶技术研究相关的文件。竞争对手提交了数百万份文件，但其中没有一份包含与制造商专利技术相关的信息。

案件进入审判阶段，陪审团作出了有利于竞争对手的裁决。在法院根据此裁决作出判决六个月后，该竞争对手的数辆自动驾驶汽车引发事故，其首席执行官（CEO）被控犯有刑事过失罪。在搜查竞争对手的研究实验室时，警方发现了数份包含制造商专利自动驾驶技术信息的文件。这些文件三年前就已保存在竞争对手的电脑中。

发现这一新证据后，该制造商可以采取什么行动？

zh-choices.A: 请求重新审判。
zh-choices.B: 请求作出法律上当然的判决。
zh-choices.C: 请求从先前的判决中获得救济。
zh-choices.D: 请求作出即决判决。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Post-Trial Motions

核心规则：FRCP 60(b) 当出现新发现的证据 (Newly Discovered Evidence) 或对方当事人的欺诈/不当行为 (Fraud/Misconduct) 时，当事人可以请求法院免除终局判决的效力 (Relief from Judgment)。

关键时限：判决作出后 1 年内。
案情时间轴分析

本题的解题关键在于“时间”。不同的审后动议有非常严格的截止日期。

Day 0
法院作出终局判决 (Entry of Judgment)
Day 28
截止：重新审判 (New Trial) & JMOL
Month 6 (当前时间)
发现新证据/对方隐瞒证据。
✔ 此时仍在 Rule 60(b) 的1年期限内。
Year 1
截止：特殊救济 (Relief from Judgment)
为什么选 C？

正确答案 C：Move for relief from the prior judgment.

根据 FRCP 60(b)，如果动议是基于以下理由，必须在判决后 1年内 提出：

  1. 错误、意外或可原谅的疏忽 (Mistake, inadvertence, excusable neglect)；
  2. 新发现的证据 (Newly discovered evidence)：该证据在审判时已存在，且尽职调查下无法及时发现；
  3. 对方的不当行为 (Fraud, misrepresentation, or misconduct)。

本案中，竞争对手在 Discovery 阶段隐瞒文件属于不当行为，且这些文件是新发现的证据。时间仅过去6个月，符合1年的时效要求。

为什么其他选项错误？
动议类型 英文名称 时限 (Deadline)
重新审判 New Trial (Rule 59) 28天
法律判决 JMOL (Rule 50) 28天
即决判决 Summary Judgment 审判前 (Pre-trial)

A 和 B 错误： 虽然新证据通常是重新审判的理由，但本案已经过了6个月，远远超过了 Rule 50 和 Rule 59 规定的 28天 严格时限。
D 错误： 即决判决只能在审判开始前提出，案件已经终审判决，不再适用。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
After being forcibly ejected from a casino, a tourist brought a federal diversity action against the casino, seeking $105,000 in damages. The tourist claimed that the casino's security guard had used excessive force when ejecting him from the casino, causing severe personal injuries.
At trial, the tourist's attorney attempted to introduce testimony of the security guard's ex-wife, who had filed several complaints of spousal abuse against the security guard. The casino's attorney objected that the evidence was irrelevant and unfairly prejudicial. The court overruled the objection, and the ex-wife testified. The jury returned a verdict for the tourist, awarding him $82,000 in damages.
The casino's attorney believes that the ex-wife's testimony was unfairly prejudicial and should not have been admitted.
What is the best way for the casino's attorney to attack the verdict?

choices.A: Appeal, arguing that the trial court erred in admitting the testimony, which was so prejudicial that the judgment should be reversed.
choices.B: Move for a new trial, arguing that the court erred in admitting the testimony and that a new trial without the testimony is necessary.
choices.C: Move for judgment as a matter of law, arguing that the court erred in admitting the testimony and that without the testimony, the evidence was legally insufficient to find for the tourist.
choices.D: Move for relief from judgment, arguing that the court's admission of the testimony was a mistake.

questions.explanation:
Grounds for new trial
  • Prejudicial trial error (eg, erroneous evidentiary ruling)
  • Prejudicial misconduct by judge, attorney, party, or juror
  • Verdict not supported by clear weight of evidence
  • Verdict based on false/nonexistent evidence
  • Excessive or inadequate damages
  • Newly discovered evidence

Within 28 days after entry of a final judgment, a party can move for a new trial on several grounds (see above image)—including that a prejudicial trial error occurred because the court erroneously admitted evidence. Here, the casino's attorney believes that the testimony by the security guard's ex-wife was unfairly prejudicial and should have been excluded. Therefore, the best way to attack the jury's verdict is to move for a new trial, arguing that the court erred in admitting the testimony and that a new trial without the testimony is necessary.

(Choice A) A party may appeal to the federal appellate court encompassing the federal district court that issued an adverse finding, conclusion, or ruling (eg, erroneously admitted evidence). But since the appellate process is time-consuming and expensive, the most immediate way to obtain the desired relief is to move for a new trial.

(Choice C) A judgment as a matter of law (JMOL) is a judgment entered in favor of the movant because the evidence is legally insufficient for a reasonable jury to find in the nonmovant's favor. However, once the jury has returned its verdict, a party can only move for a renewed JMOL if that party had moved for JMOL before the case was submitted to the jury (not seen here).

(Choice D) A party may move for relief from a final judgment in limited circumstances, including when the judgment was due to a mistake by the parties or the court. Judicial mistakes that qualify for such relief include mistakes in the entry of judgment, but not in admitting evidence. Therefore, this is not the best way to attack the verdict.

📌 Educational Objective

A motion for a new trial can be made on several grounds, including that a prejudicial trial error occurred because the trial court erroneously admitted evidence that should have been excluded.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 59 (motion for a new trial).
  • 11 Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2805 (4th ed. 2020) (explaining the grounds to move for a new trial).
questions.zh-question:
一名游客被强行逐出赌场后，对赌场提起了联邦多元管辖权诉讼，要求赔偿105,000美元。该游客声称，赌场的保安在将他逐出赌场时使用了过度武力，导致其严重人身伤害。

在庭审中，游客的律师试图引入保安前妻的证词，该前妻曾对该保安提起过数次配偶虐待的控诉。赌场律师提出异议，认为该证据无关且具有不公平的偏见性。法院驳回了异议，前妻出庭作证。陪审团作出了有利于游客的裁决，判给他82,000美元的损害赔偿金。

赌场律师认为，前妻的证词具有不公平的偏见性，本不应被采纳。

赌场律师攻击该裁决的最佳方式是什么？

zh-choices.A: 上诉，主张初审法院在采纳证词方面存在错误，该证词具有极大的偏见性，因此判决应被推翻。
zh-choices.B: 申请重新审判，主张法院在采纳证词方面存在错误，并且有必要在排除该证词的情况下进行新的审判。
zh-choices.C: 申请作出法律上的判决(judgment as a matter of law)，主张法院在采纳证词方面存在错误，并且在没有该证词的情况下，证据在法律上不足以支持有利于游客的裁决。
zh-choices.D: 申请判决补救(relief from judgment)，主张法院采纳证词是一个错误。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：审判后动议

本题考查的核心知识点是联邦民事诉讼规则（Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, FRCP）中的重新审判动议（Motion for a New Trial）。

核心考点：重新审判动议 (Rule 59)

当审判过程中出现了具有偏见性的错误（Prejudicial Error），导致审判不公平时，受损方应申请重新审判。

常见理由包括：

  • 错误的证据裁定（Erroneous evidentiary ruling）—— 本题考点
  • 法官或律师的不当行为（Misconduct）
  • 陪审团裁决严重违背证据权重（Verdict against the weight of evidence）
  • 损害赔偿金过高或过低（Excessive or inadequate damages）

✅ 正确答案分析 (选项 B)

最佳策略：申请重新审判 (Move for a New Trial)

1. 错误的性质：
本案中，法官允许引入了保安前妻关于“配偶虐待”的证词。根据证据法，这通常属于品格证据（Character Evidence），在民事案件中用于证明被告行为符合其性格通常是不可采纳的（Inadmissible），且具有极大的不公平偏见（Unfair Prejudice, FRE 403）。

2. 救济的逻辑：
既然证据已经被陪审团听到，且可能影响了裁决结果，单纯的法律判决无法修正这一过程性错误。唯一的补救方式是“重来一次”，即在排除该错误证据的情况下进行新的审判。

3. 时效性：
根据 FRCP 59，该动议必须在判决登记后 28天 内提出。这是攻击基于程序错误或证据错误的裁决最直接、最标准的途径。

❌ 为什么其他选项不是最佳？

选项 A (Appeal/上诉)：
虽然最终可以上诉，但上诉程序耗时且昂贵。法律原则要求当事人先在初审法院（Trial Court）寻求救济。如果初审法官能通过批准“重新审判”来纠正自己的错误，就不需要上诉法院介入。因此，直接上诉不是“最佳”的第一步。
选项 C (JMOL/法律判决)：
法律判决 (Judgment as a Matter of Law) 关注的是证据的充分性（Sufficiency），而不是可采性（Admissibility）。
此外，程序上有一个硬性障碍：只有在案件提交给陪审团之前已经提出了JMOL动议，才可以在裁决后提出“更新的JMOL”（Renewed JMOL）。题目未提及此前有过此动议。
选项 D (Relief from Judgment/判决救济)：
这是 FRCP 60 规定的特殊救济，通常用于纠正文书错误（Clerical mistakes）、欺诈或新发现的证据等。它不是用来纠正法官在审判中关于证据采纳的实质性法律错误的常规工具。
MBE Civil Procedure Strategy: Identify the nature of the error (Evidentiary vs. Insufficient Evidence) to choose between New Trial and JMOL.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.topic: Alteration of or Relief of a Judgment
questions.question:
A woman brought a diversity action against a pharmaceutical company in a federal court in State A for strict products liability arising under State A law. The woman claims that the company defectively manufactured her medication, which caused her to suffer a stroke that led to complete paralysis of the left side of her body.
The company moved for summary judgment, arguing that a State A statute forbids strict products liability lawsuits against pharmaceutical companies. The federal court granted the motion and entered summary judgment dismissing the woman's action with prejudice.
Fourteen days after the federal court entered summary judgment, the highest court in State A held that the State A statute granting immunity to pharmaceutical companies only applies to strict products liability actions alleging a design defect.
What is the best course of action the woman's lawyer could take?

choices.A: File a motion for judgment as a matter of law.
choices.B: File a motion to amend the summary judgment.
choices.C: File a motion to correct the mistake in the summary judgment.
choices.D: Refile the strict products liability action against the pharmaceutical company.

questions.explanation:
Motion to alter or amend final judgment
Motion must be made within 28 days on any of following grounds:
  • Judgment based on manifest error of law or fact (eg, court applied wrong law)
  • Necessary to prevent manifest injustice (eg, attorney or juror misconduct)
  • Discovery of new evidence that was unavailable during trial
  • Intervening change in controlling law

A party can file a motion to alter or amend a final judgment (eg, a summary judgment) within 28 days after entry of that judgment. This motion can be based on several grounds (see image above), including an intervening change in the controlling law.

Here, a State A federal district court entered summary judgment in favor of the pharmaceutical company because a State A statute forbade strict products liability lawsuits against pharmaceutical companies. Fourteen days later, the highest court in State A held that the statute only grants such immunity in strict products liability actions alleging a design defect. Since the woman alleges a manufacturing defect, the best course her lawyer could take is to quickly file a motion to amend the summary judgment. This will allow her case to proceed in federal court.

(Choice A) A party can move for judgment as a matter of law (JMOL) only after the nonmovant has had an opportunity to present evidence at trial (not seen here). Additionally, there is no indication that the woman has offered proof that the company defectively manufactured the medication at issue that would entitle her to JMOL.

(Choice B) A motion to correct a mistake is appropriate when a judgment contains a clerical mistake or a mistake arising from an oversight or omission. However, no such mistakes exist in the summary judgment at issue here. Instead, the summary judgment was based on substantive controlling law that has since changed.

(Choice D) The woman could refile her strict products liability action against the pharmaceutical company. However, this would not be the best way to challenge the summary judgment since this would likely be more expensive and time-consuming than moving to amend the judgment.

📌 Educational Objective

A party can move to alter or amend a final judgment, including a summary judgment, within 28 days after entry of the judgment. One ground for such a motion is that there has been an intervening change in the controlling law.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 59(e) (motion to alter or amend a judgment).
  • 47 Am. Jur. 2d Judgments § 636 (2020) (explaining the grounds for a motion to alter or amend a final judgment).

一名女士在A州联邦法院对一家制药公司提起了州际诉讼(diversity action)，该诉讼是基于A州法律下的严格产品责任(strict products liability)。该女士声称，该公司生产的药物存在制造缺陷，导致她中风，并造成其左半身完全瘫痪。

该公司动议即决判决(summary judgment)，辩称A州的一项法规禁止针对制药公司提起严格产品责任诉讼。联邦法院批准了该动议，并作出了驳回该女士诉讼且不得复诉(with prejudice)的即决判决。

该女士的律师可以采取的最佳行动方案是什么？

zh-choices.A: 提出法律问题判决(judgment as a matter of law)动议。
zh-choices.B: 提出修改即决判决的动议。
zh-choices.C: 提出纠正即决判决中错误的动议。
zh-choices.D: 重新对该制药公司提起严格产品责任诉讼。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Post-Trial Motions
⚖️ 核心规则：FRCP 59(e)

变更或修改判决的动议 (Motion to Alter or Amend a Judgment)

必须在判决录入后 28天 内提出。常见理由包括：

  • 明显的法律或事实错误 (Manifest error of law or fact)
  • 新发现的证据 (Newly discovered evidence)
  • 管辖法律的介入性变更 (Intervening change in controlling law)
案情逻辑分析

本题考察的是在判决作出后，法律依据发生变化时的程序性救济手段。

  • 现状：联邦法院基于A州法律作出了即决判决 (Summary Judgment)，驳回了原告的诉讼。
  • 变化：14天后，A州最高法院（州法律的最终解释者）澄清了法律，表明原判决依据的法律解释是错误的。
  • 时效：距离判决录入仅过去 14天，处于 FRCP 59(e) 规定的 28天 窗口期内。
  • 结论：原告律师应利用这一“管辖法律的介入性变更”，根据 Rule 59(e) 申请修改判决。这是最直接、最高效的途径。
✅ 正确答案：B

提出修改即决判决的动议 (File a motion to amend the summary judgment)

这是基于 FRCP 59(e) 的标准操作。由于联邦法院在多样性管辖 (Diversity Jurisdiction) 案件中必须适用州实体法（Erie Doctrine），当州最高法院明确指出之前的法律解释（即给予制药公司全面豁免）不适用于“制造缺陷”时，联邦法院之前的判决就失去了法律基础。及时提出动议可以撤销原判决，使案件重回正轨。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
A. 法律问题判决动议 (JMOL)

错误原因：JMOL (Rule 50) 仅适用于陪审团审判 (Jury Trial) 期间或之后。本案在即决判决阶段就结束了，根本没有进入庭审，因此不适用 JMOL。

C. 纠正错误的动议 (Correction of Mistake)

错误原因：这通常指 Rule 60(a) 下的笔误或文书错误 (Clerical Mistake)。本案中法官并非手误，而是基于当时理解的法律作出了实质性判决。虽然法律后来变了，但这不属于“文书错误”。

D. 重新提起诉讼 (Refile)

错误原因：原判决是 "With Prejudice" (不得复诉) 的终局判决。根据既判力原则 (Res Judicata / Claim Preclusion)，原告不能就同一诉因再次起诉。她必须先推翻原判决（通过动议或上诉），而不能直接重新起诉。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

看到 "Summary Judgment" 后紧接着出现 "Change in Law" 或 "New Evidence"，首先检查时间线：

  • ≤ 28天：首选 Rule 59(e) (Motion to Alter/Amend)。
  • > 28天：考虑 Rule 60(b) (Relief from Judgment)。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A purchaser filed a federal diversity action against a seller, alleging breach of contract. The seller answered the complaint and included as a separate defense an allegation that the purchaser had brought and lost a similar contract claim against a different seller three years earlier, and that this history represented a pattern of filing frivolous lawsuits. The purchaser believes that the earlier lawsuit was factually completely different from the current one and is therefore irrelevant.
What is the purchaser's best response to the seller's answer?

choices.A: File a reply that includes a denial of the separate defense.
choices.B: Move for sanctions against the seller for asserting a frivolous defense.
choices.C: Move to amend the complaint to add allegations about the differences between the lawsuits.
choices.D: Move to strike the separate defense as irrelevant.

questions.explanation:
FRCP 12 motions
12(b) Motion asserting any of the following defenses:
  • Lack of subject-matter or personal jurisdiction
  • Improper venue
  • Insufficient process or service of process
  • Failure to state claim upon which relief can be granted
  • Failure to join required party
12(c) Motion for judgment on the pleadings
12(e) Motion for more definite statement in pleading
12(f) Motion to strike insufficient defense or immaterial matter from pleading

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 12(f), a party may move to strike an insufficient defense or any redundant, scandalous, impertinent, or immaterial matter from an opposing party's pleading. A party must make this motion:

  • before responding to the pleading if a response is allowed (eg, when the defendant's answer contains a counterclaim or the court orders a reply) or
  • within 21 days after being served with the pleading if a response is not allowed.*

Here, the purchaser believes that the seller's separate defense is irrelevant (ie, immaterial). Therefore, the purchaser's best response is to move to strike this defense from the answer. The motion must be filed within 21 days after the seller's answer was served because the answer does not contain a counterclaim and the court has not ordered a reply.

*The court may also strike defenses and matters in pleadings at any time on its own initiative (ie, sua sponte).

(Choice A) A reply is a response to an answer that can only be filed pursuant to a court order (not seen here).

(Choice B) A court may impose sanctions on a party that asserts a frivolous claim or defense—ie, one that has no factual or legal basis and was asserted to harass, delay, or embarrass. Since there is no indication that the seller asserted the defense for any of these illegitimate purposes, the court is unlikely to grant a motion for sanctions.

(Choice C) A plaintiff may move to amend the complaint to correct errors and omissions, allege new claims, or change the defendant. However, an amendment to respond to allegations in the defendant's answer is not allowed.

📌 Educational Objective

A party can move to strike from a pleading an insufficient defense or any redundant, scandalous, impertinent, or immaterial matter. A party must make this motion (1) before responding to the pleading or (2) within 21 days after being served with the pleading if a response is not allowed.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(f) (motion to strike).

买方对卖方提起了一项联邦多元管辖权诉讼，指控其违约。卖方对起诉状作出了答辩，并在其中包含一项单独的抗辩，指控买方曾在三年前对另一名卖方提起过类似的合同索赔但败诉，并称这段历史表明买方存在滥诉模式。买方认为，早前的诉讼在事实上与本案完全不同，因此不具相关性。

买方对卖方的答辩状应作出的最佳回应是什么？

zh-choices.A: 提交一份复辩状，其中包含对该单独抗辩的否认。
zh-choices.B: 动议因卖方提出无聊的抗辩而对其进行制裁。
zh-choices.C: 动议修改起诉状，以增加关于两起诉讼之间差异的指控。
zh-choices.D: 动议以不具相关性为由删除该单独的抗辩。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure (民事诉讼法)
最佳选项 (Correct Answer)
D. 动议以不具相关性为由删除该单独的抗辩。
Move to strike the separate defense as irrelevant.
本题的核心考点在于如何处理诉答文书（Pleadings）中出现的无关或不当内容。
法律依据：FRCP 12(f)

根据《联邦民事诉讼规则》第12(f)条，法院可以（依职权或依当事人动议）从诉答文书中删除任何不充分的抗辩 (insufficient defense)，或者任何冗余 (redundant)、无关紧要 (immaterial)、不相关 (impertinent) 或诽谤性 (scandalous) 的事项。

逻辑分析：
在本案中，被告（卖方）在答辩状中提到的“买方3年前针对另一卖方的败诉经历”，与当前的违约诉讼在事实和法律上均无关联。
  • 这属于典型的无关紧要事项 (Immaterial Matter)。
  • 它对本案的判决结果没有法律上的影响，且可能意在抹黑原告。
因此，原告（买方）最恰当的程序性应对措施是根据 Rule 12(f) 提出删除动议 (Motion to Strike)。

为什么其他选项是错误的？

  • 选项 A：提交复辩状 (File a reply) 错误。 根据 FRCP 7(a)，除非法院明确命令，否则原告不得对被告的答辩状（Answer）提交复辩状。原告不能仅仅因为想反驳就自行提交 Reply。
  • 选项 B：动议制裁 (Move for sanctions) 错误。 虽然该抗辩无关紧要，但要达到 Rule 11 制裁的标准（即完全无理取闹、恶意骚扰或毫无根据），门槛非常高。此外，制裁动议有特定的程序要求（如“安全港”原则），并不是处理无关抗辩的“最佳”或首选方式。
  • 选项 C：修改起诉状 (Amend the complaint) 错误。 修改起诉状是为了修正原告自己的主张或增加事实，而不是用来反驳被告答辩状中的指控。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

当你看到题目中描述诉答文书（Pleading）里包含了"scandalous"（诽谤性）、"irrelevant"（不相关）或"prejudicial"（有偏见）的内容时，第一反应应当是寻找 Motion to Strike (Rule 12(f))。

时间限制： 如果是对答辩状提出此动议，必须在送达后 21天 内提出。
